Predict one real person's current choice in the Formula condition of Crosetto and Mantovani's centipede experiment. The experiment took place in German; this is an English rendering of its instructions. Two people have fixed roles White and Black. White acts at decision rounds1,3,5,7,9,11 and Black at2,4,6,8,10,12. At each reached decision round, the actor chooses STOP or CONTINUE. STOP ends this game. CONTINUE passes the decision to the other person. If everyone continues through decision round12, the game ends automatically at round13; there is no thirteenth choice.

Formula payoff information: when a player chooses STOP at decision round r, that player receives four times the current round, V_STOP = 4 × r. The other player receives one times the current round, V_OTHER = 1 × r. This treatment supplies the rule and algebra; future payoffs must be worked out by the participant. Do not replace this information with the complete terminal-payoff tree or a table of all future payoffs. Each active screen also shows the current round and the two amounts if the current actor stops; inactive players see the current round and those same current STOP amounts. These current amounts are provided in the user message.

Each decision allows30seconds. A player may revise a choice within those30seconds; pressing OK makes the choice final. The recorded target is that final choice. You play12games in the same role. Each game pairs you with a new person, never the same partner twice; your partners do not play each other. You can proceed at your pair's pace within a game but wait for others between games. After all12games, the computer randomly selects one game for payment. Earnings use experimental currency units (ECU);1ECU equals1euro. You also receive a2.5euro show-up fee. No particular payment draw or final profit is known at the current decision.

All participants had to answer the control questions correctly before playing. Current target answers, later moves and games, final payment, postgame risk/trust/complexity answers and the anonymous partner's demographics are unavailable. Earlier completed games describe only your already experienced actions and outcomes; they do not reveal this new partner's history. Reply with exactly STOP or CONTINUE, without explanation.

The experiment took place in German; this is an English rendering of its instructions. Two people have fixed roles White and Black. White acts at decision rounds1,3,5,7,9,11 and Black at2,4,6,8,10,12. At each reached decision round, the actor chooses STOP or CONTINUE. STOP ends this game. CONTINUE passes the decision to the other person. If everyone continues through decision round12, the game ends automatically at round13; there is no thirteenth choice.

Formula payoff information: when a player chooses STOP at decision round r, that player receives four times the current round, V_STOP = 4 × r. The other player receives one times the current round, V_OTHER = 1 × r. This treatment supplies the rule and algebra; future payoffs must be worked out by the participant. Do not replace this information with the complete terminal-payoff tree or a table of all future payoffs. Each active screen also shows the current round and the two amounts if the current actor stops; inactive players see the current round and those same current STOP amounts. These current amounts are provided in the user message.

Each decision allows30seconds. A player may revise a choice within those30seconds; pressing OK makes the choice final. The recorded target is that final choice. You play12games in the same role. Each game pairs you with a new person, never the same partner twice; your partners do not play each other. You can proceed at your pair's pace within a game but wait for others between games. After all12games, the computer randomly selects one game for payment. Earnings use experimental currency units (ECU);1ECU equals1euro. You also receive a2.5euro show-up fee. No particular payment draw or final profit is known at the current decision.

After all12games, the computer randomly selects one game for payment. Earnings use experimental currency units (ECU);1ECU equals1euro. You also receive a2.5euro show-up fee. No particular payment draw or final profit is known at the current decision.
